title: Second monitor not detected
symptom: Second monitor shows nothing and Windows does not see it
user_description: I plugged in the second monitor you gave me but it stays black. Windows doesn't seem to know it is there.

options.why: Never a first step for a display problem. It wastes hours and erases settings.
Costly and premature. Nothing has been tested yet, so the card is unlikely to be the cause.

options.text: Check the cable and the monitor's input, try a different port or cable, then in Display settings use Detect or press Windows key + P and choose Extend
options.why: This works from simple to complex: physical connection first, then asking Windows to look for the screen, then choosing how to use it. Many 'not detected' cases are a loose cable or a wrong display mode.
Risky and rarely needed for a second screen. Try the simple checks before touching firmware.

hints: Is the monitor powered on and set to the right input?
Can you tell Windows to look for the screen again?
How does Windows decide whether to copy, extend or show only one screen?
real_world_tip: Try the monitor on another port of the PC. If one port works and another does not, you know the port is the problem.
